comparisons.peer_summary: The graphics market is driven by AI, VR/AR, and high-resolution gaming needs; the company announced GDDR7 in 2024, completing its industry-leading portfolio for AI inference on CPUs, NPUs, and GPUs.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies operate in the graphics hardware ecosystem but at different supply chain layers. AMD manufactures and markets professional GPU products (Radeon PRO) that utilize memory, whereas Micron manufactures the underlying GDDR graphics DRAM and memory modules (GDDR6, GDDR7) that are incorporated into PC graphics cards and data center GPU solutions. Micron notes its graphics products are driving force behind applications such as AI and professional design, which aligns with AMD's target market for its professional GPUs, though AMD is the OEM/product brand and Micron is the component supplier.

sentences.text: Our AMD Radeon PRO family of professional graphics products are designed for integration in desktop workstations, optimized through hardware and software for demanding use cases such as 3D rendering, design and manufacturing for Computer-Aided Design (CAD), and media and entertainment for broadcast and animation pipelines on high resolution displays.

Our GDDR6 and GDDR6X DRAM graphics products are incorporated into gaming consoles, PC graphics cards, and graphics processing unit-based data center solutions, which are the driving force behind applications such as AI, virtual and augmented reality, 4K and 8K gaming, and professional design.
The addition of GDDR7 completes our industry-leading product portfolio for AI inference applications on CPUs, neural processing units, and graphics processing units.

comparisons.peer_summary: GDDR is a high-performance memory solution optimized for high-bandwidth workloads in graphics cards, gaming consoles, and high-performance computing applications.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison links AMD's end-product graphics cards to Micron's component-level supply. AMD's Radeon PRO family provides professional graphics products for workstations, which inherently require high-bandwidth memory. Micron explicitly describes its GDDR memory as a high-performance memory solution designed for graphics cards and optimized for high-bandwidth workloads encountered by GPUs. While AMD sells the integrated graphics solution, Micron provides the critical memory component that enables the high-performance graphics capabilities AMD markets.
